output.answer: Yes. On November 9, 2026, PepsiCo confirmed — via an internal letter to employees from PepsiCo North America CEO Ram Krishnan, first reported by The Wall Street Journal — that it will cut about 1,000 jobs across its North American food and beverage operations over the following week, as it seeks to streamline operations and better connect teams amid lagging home-market sales. The layoffs follow PepsiCo's October 2026 cut to its full-year 2026 earnings outlook, after Q3 North American beverage volume fell 2% and food volume was flat. They are part of a broader cost-reduction push announced in December 2025 (three U.S. manufacturing plant closures and a roughly 20% U.S. SKU reduction) following engagement with shareholder Elliott Investment Management. PepsiCo has not issued a public press release on the layoffs; the ~1,000 figure comes from the internal letter as reported by CNBC, Fox Business and others.

The cuts are described as "about 1,000" jobs across North America only; details such as which teams, locations or severance terms were not disclosed.

PepsiCo lowered its full-year 2026 earnings outlook in October 2026 and has said it will provide a comprehensive update on North America supply chain and go-to-market optimization in late 2026, so further restructuring actions are possible.

passages.quote: [PepsiCo](https://www.cnbc.com/quotes/PEP/) is cutting about 1,000 jobs across North America as the company tries to turn around lagging sales in its home market.

"We have a clear ambition for PepsiCo North America: to build a stronger, more future-fit business that delivers industry-leading growth," Ram Krishnan, CEO of PepsiCo North America, wrote in a Monday letter to employees obtained by CNBC. "To do that, we need to be faster, more connected, and more capable, while continuing to invest in growth — behind our people, capabilities and brands."

Over the next week, Pepsi plans to cut jobs as it says it aims to streamline its operations and better connect teams across the company's North American business. PepsiCo employs about 306,000 people worldwide, including roughly 125,000 in the United States, as of Dec. 27, according to a company filing.

The [planned layoffs](https://www.foxbusiness.com/category/jobs), first reported by The Wall Street Journal, come after PepsiCo lowered its full-year 2026 earnings outlook in October, citing challenges in its North American business, including weaker beverage sales volumes, pressure on snack demand and higher costs.

The reductions are expected to take place over the next week, according to an internal letter from PepsiCo North America [CEO Ram Krishnan](https://www.foxbusiness.com/business-leaders) obtained by Reuters.

*   **Aggressively reducing operating costs** and **improving operational excellence** with savings generated to support meaningful investments in advertising and marketing and consumer value. For example, we have closed three manufacturing plants and shut several manufacturing lines this year and are in the process of reducing nearly 20 percent of SKUs in the U.S. by early next year.
